evidence.note: Agent searches cargo for existing C compilers (chibicc, wrecc) and reads wrecc_compiler source rather than designing a pipeline — architecture is sought externally, not authored.

Copies wrecc include dir and vendors the entire wrecc_compiler crate into /app/compiler; the staged lexer/preprocessor/parser/typechecker/codegen pipeline and all type/scope representations are inherited wholesale, not designed by the agent.

Agent studies the borrowed architecture (types.rs, token.rs, parser HIR, scanner, preprocessor) to understand where to patch — architectural comprehension of an inherited design, not design work of its own.

The entire remainder is patching the pre-existing structure (fold.rs, typechecker MIR, codegen LIR, scanner) feature-by-feature; no up-front representation design or design rationale is ever produced by the agent.

reasoning: The final artifact contains a coherent, well-layered pipeline (HIR/MIR/LIR, typed/sized values, struct layout), but that structure was vendored from the third-party wrecc_compiler crate, not designed by the agent. The agent's own architecture-design meta-work consisted only of selecting a mature pipeline and reading it to place patches — above the 0 anchor's total absence of architectural intent and comparable to the 3 anchor's 'rough separation with improvised structures,' but well short of the 5/8 anchors, which require the agent to design the staged pipeline and its representations. Because the design was inherited rather than authored, I place the observed level at 3.
